column3: “A pair of donkeys” is rendered “a couple of saddled donkeys,” and “skin of wine” as “jug of wine.”
“What are these to you?” is rendered “Why do you have these?”
“The son of your master” is rendered “your master’s son.”
“I bow down” is rendered “I prostrate myself.”
“Clan” is rendered “family.”
“Stoned with stones” is rendered “threw stones at.”
“Man of bloods” is rendered “man of bloodshed,” and “man of worthlessness” as “worthless fellow.”
“Here you are in your calamity” is rendered “you are taken in your own evil.”
“Remove his head” is rendered “cut off his head.”
The Hebrew written text reads “thus he curses, for”; NASB renders “If he curses, and if,” following the reading tradition.
“From my inward parts” is rendered “from me.”
The Hebrew written text reads “on my iniquity” (the reading tradition “my eye”); NASB renders “my affliction,” as in some ancient versions.
“Dusted with dust” is rendered “threw dust at him.”
NASB supplies “arrived.” The Hebrew may name a place (“Ayephim”) rather than “weary.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“May the king live” is rendered “Long live the king!”

NASB adds “Should I not serve.”
“Give counsel for yourselves” is rendered “Give your advice.”
